key_insight: Trustworthy protein–ligand binding predictions require trustworthy evaluation. This paper advocates transparent data, code and experimental procedures so scoring methods can be compared fairly and reproducibly.
problem_solved: Data leakage, biased benchmarks and unclear evaluation procedures can inflate apparent performance, obscuring how well protein–ligand scoring methods actually generalize.
method: Promote transparent reporting and sharing of evaluation data, code and experimental procedures.
Recommend good practices to prevent data leakage and reduce bias in evaluation.
Encourage consistent evaluation practices that enable fair, reproducible and meaningful comparisons across scoring methods.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, these guidelines support more credible benchmarking and model selection. They help distinguish genuine predictive progress from gains caused by leakage or biased evaluation.
visual_elements: Protein–ligand illustration showing a small molecule fitting into a protein binding pocket.
Train–test split diagram with a blocked arrow representing prevention of data leakage.
Transparency checklist with icons for data, code and experimental procedures.
Side-by-side evaluation panels contrasting biased benchmarking with fair, reproducible comparison.
paper_title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
